newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arabs, Moslems urge world action on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Arabs, Moslems urge world action on Jerusalem.

text.p: Arab and Moslem officials on Monday slammed Israel for its policies on Jerusalem, which they said were driving away dozens of Palestinian residents and endangering the Middle East peace process.

They were speaking at a "Day of Unity with Jerusalem" event organised by the Arab League and the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC) to commemorate Israel's annexation of Arab East Jerusalem on June 28, 1970, three years after the occupation.
In a speech read by the Palestinian representative to the Arab League, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said there would never be peace unless the status of Jerusalem was resolved.
"Peace begins in Jerusalem, the land of peace. There will be no peace without Jerusalem, the land of religions," Arafat said.
"I call on our Arab and Islamic nations to combat the crime of Judaisation of Jerusalem and to stand up to the settlement attack on Jerusalem -- the eternal capital of Palestine."
Talks between the Palestinians and Israel collapsed in March when the Jewish state began building a new settlement in Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa in Arab East Jersualem.
Palestinians say such measures prejudge the outcome of final status talks that are meant to resolve the thorniest issues of the peace talks, such as the status of the disputed city.
Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its eternal capital, while the Palestinians hope its eastern part will one day be the capital of an independent state.

"(Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu's government has insisted on applying its settlement policy and has concentrated its attack on Jerusalem in particular, in order to hit the peace process," Arafat said. "The policy of Netanyahu's government is pushing the situation to explosion."

"In spite of the sincere efforts by us, our Arab brothers and international friends to overcome the obstacles that face the peace process, Netanyahu's government insists on continuing the policy of imposing a de facto reality in holy Jerusalem and other parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip," he added.

Arafat and others at the event also condemned a resolution by the U.S. House of Representatives in June recognising Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and recommending Washington move its embassy from Tel Aviv to the disputed city.

"All these positions and measures cast doubt on the credibility of the United States as a true sponsor of the peace process and as a genuine partner in the process," said Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid in a speech read by a senior league official.
"Such clear bias that supports confiscation and destruction of all that is Palestinian in the city of Jerusalem creates an atmosphere of mistrust," he added.
Officials at the event urged Israel to heed a non-binding U.N. General Assembly resolution that urged the Jewish state to stop building settlements on occupied Arab land.

"The occupying Israeli authorities do not realise what goes on in the heart of every Arab and Moslem of this and other generations," said a speech by OIC Secretary General Ezzeldine al-Iraqi, read by an OIC official.

"Any peace that does not restore Jerusalem will continue to be rejected because the love of Jerusalem, connection to it and the wish to defend it is a deeply rooted article of faith that is born and develops with each Moslem. This eternal connection will not be affected by Israeli resolutions or practices."
